correctness.rationale: Naskręcki, arXiv:2108.13402 Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 3.1, establishes all 800 irreducible conics and precisely 400 supporting planes; the two cutting-plane seeds and four printed generators are exact. The accompanying self-contained script computes all 160+240=400 distinct normalized dual rows over Q(i,sqrt5), checks closure under all four Galois automorphisms, verifies fixed counts 64,160,16 for the three involutions, and counts all 400 stabilizers. The equality of normalized rows is exact rational field arithmetic. The Gal(K/Q) subgroup-fixed-field correspondence yields 16,144,48,192 and 16+96+48 Galois orbits. Published geometric completeness is an explicit premise; no finite sampling extrapolation or assertion about component fields is made.

originality.rationale: The closest primary source already proves 800 conics and 400 conic-pair hyperplanes and prints the group generators and seeds, but gives neither the minimal fields of the 400 supporting planes nor their Galois stabilizer profile. The geometric Kummer and maximal-conics classifications also do not imply these arithmetic strata in their inspected statements. Targeted searches for fields, conjugation, Galois orbits and exact counts found no equivalent record; the residual risk of implicit older or supplemental calculations is expressly acknowledged.
residual_risks: An older, unindexed arithmetic calculation or supplementary computer-algebra files might encode the same 400-plane descent census implicitly.

Failure of a finite set of bibliographic searches does not establish global novelty; the exact claim is limited to embedded planes and must not be read as a claim about individual conic component fields.

value.rationale: The full geometrically conic-splitting hyperplane locus of the unique maximal-conic quartic is a distinguished finite arithmetic scheme over Q. Its individual rational/imaginary-quadratic/real-quadratic/biquadratic descent and Galois permutation type are natural exact invariants needed to distinguish geometric decompositions visible over Q from conic components visible only after further extension. The claim is a complete 400-element classification using the natural plane objects and does not recompute merely the published number 800 or 400. The precise arithmetic field split is motivated independently of downstream conjectures.
